'''Chukwuebuka Ejiofor''' (born April 20, 2004) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Atlanta Hawks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]] and [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's Red Storm]].

==Early life and high school career==
Ejiofor attended [[Garland High School]] in [[Garland, Texas]], where he averaged 21 points and 13 rebounds per game as a [[Junior (education year)|junior]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bedore |first1=Gary |title=Former KU forward Zuby Ejiofor picks transfer spot ... with another Hall of Fame coach |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article275434586.html |website=Kansas City Star |access-date=10 March 2025}}</ref> As a [[Senior (education)|senior]], he averaged 22 points, 13 rebounds, four blocks and two steals per game.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bedore |first1=Gary |title=KU Jayhawks power forward Zuby Ejiofor erupts for 28 points in Bill Self campers game |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article262546922.html |website=Kansas City Star |access-date=10 March 2025}}</ref> Coming out of high school, Ejiofor was rated as a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to play [[college basketball]] for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Guskey |first1=Jordan |title='I saw the opportunities': Catching up with Kansas men's basketball commit Zuby Ejiofor |url=https://www.cjonline.com/story/sports/college/hawk-zone/2021/10/25/zuby-ejiofor-kansas-basketball-2022-recruiting-class-get-know-commit-gradey-dick-mj-rice/6121813001/ |website=The Topeka Capital-Journal |access-date=10 March 2025}}</ref>

==College career==
=== Kansas ===
On December 17, 2022, Ejiofor put up eight points, two rebounds, and a block in a win over [[2022–23 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|Indiana]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Laddha |first1=Shreyas |title=How Kansas Jayhawks freshman Zuby Ejiofor made most of opportunity against Indiana |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article270140307.html |website=Kansas City Star |access-date=10 March 2025}}</ref> He finished his [[freshman]] season in 2022–23 appearing in 25 games, where he averaged 1.2 points and 1.7 rebounds in 5.2 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Guskey |first1=Jordan |title=Kansas men's basketball forward Zuby Ejiofor has entered the transfer portal |url=https://www.cjonline.com/story/sports/college/hawk-zone/2023/05/05/zuby-ejiofor-will-transfer-from-kansas-mens-basketball-program/70188672007/ |website=The Topeka Capital-Journal |access-date=10 March 2025}}</ref> 

At the end of Ejiofor’s freshman year, Kansas head coach [[Bill Self]] wanted him to redshirt for a year. Self told Ejiofor and his father, Andy Philachack, that he wasn’t “good enough to start and/or play major minutes on any Big 12 team.” The conversation led Ejiofor to transfer. His father later said: “The conversation was pretty serious, Zuby didn’t like it at all. Basically Zuby was like, ‘I didn’t even get a chance.’ Telling him he’s not good enough to play, that put a fire in (Zuby). It was like, ‘All right Dad, get me out of here.’”

After the season, Ejiofor entered his name into the [[NCAA transfer portal]],<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bedore |first1=Gary |title=Zuby Ejiofor's mentor and KU coach Bill Self discuss freshman entering transfer portal |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article275107161.html |website=Kansas City Star |access-date=10 March 2025}}</ref> and later transferred to play for the [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's Red Storm]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Serby |first1=Steve |title=Zuby Ejiofor's March Madness dreams fueling his St. John's rise after heartbreaking end last year |url=https://nypost.com/2024/12/28/sports/zuby-ejiofors-march-madness-dreams-fueling-his-st-johns-rise/ |website=New York Post |access-date=10 March 2025}}</ref> By the end of his time at St. John's, he was projected to be drafted early in the 2nd round of the NBA draft, a level that most Big 12 starters don't reach. In the 2026 NCAA tournament Round of 32, he helped St. John’s beat his former team, Kansas, and his former coach to advance the school to the Sweet 16 for the first time in 25 years.<ref>{{Cite web |last=NJ.com |first=Adam Zagoria {{!}} For |date=2026-03-03 |title=How does St. John’s star project to the pros? ‘Amazing how he has improved’ |url=https://www.nj.com/sports/2026/03/how-does-st-johns-star-project-to-the-pros-nba-scouts-react.html |access-date=2026-03-29 |website=nj |language=en}}</ref> 

Before the game, Self said: “We didn’t want him to leave. We’re really happy for his success. We just hope it doesn’t come against us.” 

=== St. John's ===
In his junior and senior years at St. John’s, Ejiofor led St. John’s to consecutive Big East regular season championships and tournament championships. In his senior year, he was chosen as the Big East Defensive Player of the Year, and the unanimous choice for conference Player of the Year. He was the first ever St. John's player to receive both honors in one year. He was a key reason why St. John’s finished the season ranked number 10 in the country. He was also named the winner of the Big East Scholar-Athlete of the Year, making him only the 2nd player in Big East history to win all three awards in one year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Braziller |first=Zach |date=2026-03-11 |title=Zuby Ejiofor's St. John's legend grows with Big East Player of the Year honor |url=https://nypost.com/2026/03/11/sports/zuby-ejiofors-st-johns-legend-grows-with-big-east-player-of-the-year-honor/ |access-date=2026-03-29 |website=New York Post |language=en-US}}</ref> 

At the time of the academic award, the Big East wrote that: "He is averaging 16.0 points, 7.1 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 2.0 blocks per game for the Red Storm this season. He is the only power conference player to rank top 10 in his respective conference and lead his team in all four of those statistical categories."<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-03-11 |title=St. John’s Ejiofor Named Men's Basketball Scholar-Athlete of the Year |url=https://www.bigeast.com/news/2026/3/10/st-johns-ejiofor-named-mens-basketball-scholar-athlete-of-the-year.aspx |access-date=2026-03-29 |website=www.bigeast.com |language=en}}</ref>  

In his senior year, Ejiofor was also selected as a finalist for the Kareem Abdul-Jabbar Center of the Year, and named one of four finalists for the national Naismith Trophy Defensive Player of the Year award, presented at the Final Four. He ranked 2nd in the conference and 18th in the country with 2.2 blocks per game. He also set the record for the most blocked shots in a Big East Tournament Championship game with 7 against Connecticut.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Zuby Ejiofor Named Naismith Defensive Player of the Year Finalist |url=https://redstormsports.com/news/2026/3/27/mens-basketball-zuby-ejiofor-named-naismith-defensive-player-of-the-year-finalist |access-date=2026-03-29 |website=St. John's University Athletics |language=en}}</ref> 

During the 2023-24 season, he averaged 4.3 points, 3.1 rebounds and 1.1 blocks per game.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Williams |first1=James |title=Zuby Ejiofor and Kadary Richmond Named Basketball Captains |url=https://www.torchonline.com/sports/2024/10/12/kadary-richmond-zuby-ejiofor/ |website=The Torch |access-date=10 March 2025}}</ref> On December 7, 2024, Ejiofor notched 28 points and 13 rebounds in win against [[2024–25 Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball team|Kansas State]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bedore |first1=Gary |title=Former KU basketball forward Zuby Ejiofor enjoying stellar season at St. John's |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article297564493.html |website=Kansas City Star |access-date=10 March 2025}}</ref> On December 20, he recorded 19 points and 10 rebounds, including the game-winning shot in a 72–70 win versus [[2024–25 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Providence]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Braziler |first1=Zach |title=St. John's shocks Providence at the buzzer on Zuby Ejiofor's clutch shot |url=https://nypost.com/2024/12/20/sports/st-johns-shocks-providence-at-the-buzzer-on-zuby-ejiofors-clutch-shot/ |website=New York Post |access-date=10 March 2025}}</ref> On February 26, 2025, Ejiofor finished with 12 points, four rebounds and three assists in a victory against [[2024–25 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team|Butler]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Braziler |first1=Zach |title=St. John's Zuby Ejiofor comes up big down stretch after early woes |url=https://nypost.com/2025/02/27/sports/st-johns-zuby-ejiofor-comes-up-big-down-stretch-after-early-woes/ |website=New York Post |access-date=10 March 2025}}</ref> On March 8, he scored 17 points while bringing down 12 rebounds and hitting the game-winning shot in overtime in a win over [[2024–25 Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Marquette]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Steele |first1=Ben |title=Zuby Ejiofor's shot at OT buzzer for St. John's ruins Senior Day for Kam Jones, Marquette |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/marquette/2025/03/08/marquette-vs-st-johns-live-coverage-from-fiserv-forum-in-milwaukee-for-big-east-showdown/81982001007/ |website=Milwaukee Journal-Sentinel |access-date=10 March 2025}}</ref> For his performance during the 2024–25 season, Ejiofor was named a first-team all-[[Big East Conference]] selection.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Braziler |first1=Zach |title=St. John's Zuby Ejiofor, RJ Luis make All-Big East First Team — though other star is snubbed |url=https://nypost.com/2025/03/09/sports/st-johns-zuby-ejiofor-rj-luis-make-all-big-east-first-team/ |website=New York Post |access-date=10 March 2025}}</ref>

St. John’s coach [[Rick Pitino]] praised Ejiofor, saying: “Zuby’s always trying to get better. He’s always talking about his teammates. He’s an all-American off the court because it’s all about his teammates. It’s never about him. He’s a huge throwback to what you see with young athletes today. It’s never about him. It’s always about the teammates. It’s always about St. John’s. He’s a great throwback. I’m going to miss him terribly."<ref>{{Cite web |last=read |first=Adam Zagoria·5 min |date=2026-03-21 |title=Bill Self told St. John’s star Zuby Ejiofor he ‘wasn’t good enough to start’ at Kansas |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/bill-self-told-st-john-181551682.html |access-date=2026-03-29 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

During Ejiofor's final Big East tournament, Seton Hall's head coach, [[Shaheen Holloway]], told him: “Zuby, I’m glad you’re getting out of the league. Zuby embodies what the Big East is all about. I don’t like playing against you, but I’m a big fan of yours.”<ref>{{Cite web |last=FITZPATRICK |first=By MIKE |date=2026-03-11 |title=Zuby Ejiofor, Shaheen Holloway and Nigel James Jr. take top Big East awards |url=https://www.sfgate.com/sports/article/zuby-ejiofor-shaheen-holloway-and-nigel-james-22070896.php |access-date=2026-03-29 |website=SFGATE |language=en}}</ref> 

After the 2025–26 season, Ejiofor was awarded the [[Haggerty Award]] as the top player in the New York City metro area.<ref>{{cite web|title= Zuby Ejiofor Wins Lt. Frank J. Haggerty Award|url= https://redstormsports.com/news/2026/4/23/mens-basketball-zuby-ejiofor-wins-lt-frank-j-haggerty-award |date=April 23, 2026 |publisher= [[St. John's Red Storm]] |accessdate = April 26, 2026}}</ref>

==Professional career==
On June 23, 2026, Ejiofor was selected with the 23rd overall pick by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in the [[2026 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wfaa.com/article/sports/nba/garlands-zuby-ejiofor-celebrates-nba-dream-after-hawks-select-him-in-the-first-round/287-b54db7cf-b5c9-409a-8b52-742e00634c9f|title=Garland’s Zuby Ejiofor celebrates NBA dream after Hawks select him in the first round|website=WFAA|last=Panicker|first=Jobin|date=June 24, 2026|access-date=July 15, 2026}}</ref>
